findings: Only one-bar shift: 126 shared predicted closes have 6.61–11.79bp mean parent-centered RMS disagreement across eight research cells; not a price-offset-only artifact or numerical batch noise.

Mean-prediction error is 74.80–90.01% of mean true shape MSE at shift1, and 56.24–70.79% at shift64. This is an arithmetic decomposition, not common latent information, causal effect or removable error percentage.

At shift64 the SAME63 historical closes move from ages1..63 in A to ages65..127 in B. Later shape MSE increases in all8 research cells under both cluster intervals; this is independently re-encoded rolling context, not a recurrent forgetting experiment.

Shift1 correction is mixed; shift16 later deterioration has both-cluster support in7/8 cells. Do not claim every update is worse or compare shifts as a pure dose curve: each shift selects a different common span.
Price common/entered/leaving beat flat in72/72 descriptive comparisons; the MSE gain97.90–99.93% is against a weak baseline and is NOT reconstruction accuracy or information retained.

Activity entered/leaving five fields beat fixed train-mean baselines in240/240 supported two-cluster comparisons; body40/48, with8 inconclusive and no confirmed worse under both. These correlated comparisons are not independent successes or overall acceptance.
D does not automatically replace Macro. Source training histories differ; previously confirmed D/A original-loss reconstruction gains do not imply physical shape/overlap superiority over Macro.
